# Map of Monotropic Experiences

> A map you can find yourself on. Twenty areas of monotropic experience, mapped by Helen Edgar (Autistic Realms) and developed with the Stimpunks Foundation. CC BY-SA 4.0.

Monotropism is a neurodiversity-affirming theory of autism (Murray, Lesser & Lawson, 2005): monotropic minds pull more attention toward fewer interests at a time. This site maps what that is like, area by area, and names who coined each one.

## The map
- [The map](https://monotropicmap.org/): the map itself, as a picture and as a list.
- [The twenty areas](https://monotropicmap.org/areas): grouped into flow, connection, stuck states, and pressure.
- [The frame](https://monotropicmap.org/neuronormative-domination): why stuck states are produced rather than personal.

## The twenty areas
- [Attention Tunnels](https://monotropicmap.org/attention-tunnels): Your attention goes deep into one thing. The rest of the world fades out. It feels good, and it helps you think. Coming back out again is hard. Named by Fergus Murray.
- [Penguin Pebbling Cove of Friendship](https://monotropicmap.org/penguin-pebbling-cove-of-friendship): You send someone a small thing you found. A link, a photo, a funny picture. It means: I was thinking about you. It is a way of saying love. Named by Helen Edgar.
- [Tendril Theory](https://monotropicmap.org/tendril-theory): When you focus, your mind reaches out like lots of vines. To stop, you have to pull every vine back in. That takes time. Being rushed hurts. Named by Erin Human.
- [Mountains of Ruminating Thoughts](https://monotropicmap.org/mountains-of-ruminating-thoughts): The same thought goes round and round. You cannot put it down. It gets in the way, and it can leave you tired or cross. Named by Dusty Chipura.
- [Cyclones of Unmet Needs](https://monotropicmap.org/cyclones-of-unmet-needs): You asked for help and did not get it. The gap between what you need and what you are given keeps growing. Named by Cassidy et al..
- [Rabbit Holes of Research](https://monotropicmap.org/rabbit-holes-of-research): You start looking one thing up. Hours later you are still going. You end up knowing a great deal about it.
- [Infodump Canyon](https://monotropicmap.org/infodump-canyon): You tell someone everything about a thing you love. All of the detail. This is a gift, not a lecture.
- [Rhizomatic Communities](https://monotropicmap.org/rhizomatic-communities): Lots of small Autistic groups, all joined up. Nobody is in charge. If one group stops, the rest carry on. Named by Helen Edgar.
- [River of Monotropic Flow States](https://monotropicmap.org/river-of-monotropic-flow-states): You are deep in something and time goes soft. Your body settles. This is how a monotropic person gets energy back. Named by Fergus Murray.
- [Campsite of Cavendish Spaces](https://monotropicmap.org/campsite-of-cavendish-spaces): A place that fits your body and your senses. Somewhere you can work, rest, or be with people without it costing you. Named by Ryan Boren.
- [Meerkat Mounds](https://monotropicmap.org/meerkat-mounds): You are watching for danger all the time. You cannot settle into anything. This happens when a place does not feel safe. Named by Tanya Adkin & David Gray-Hammond.
- [River Banks of Monotropic Time](https://monotropicmap.org/river-banks-of-monotropic-time): Deep focus changes time. An hour can feel like ten minutes. The outside world melts away for a while. Named by Helen Edgar.
- [Shark Infested Waters of Neuronormativity and Behaviourism & Double Empathy Problems](https://monotropicmap.org/shark-infested-waters): The water around everything else. It is the idea that there is one right way to have a mind. It is in schools, jobs and doctors' rooms. Named by Damian Milton.
- [Beach of Body Doubling](https://monotropicmap.org/beach-of-body-doubling): Someone sits nearby while you work. They do not help you and they do not watch you. Having them there makes it easier to start. Named by Jessica McCabe.
- [Burnout Whirlpools](https://monotropicmap.org/burnout-whirlpools): You have run on empty for years. Now things you used to do are too hard. Rest on its own does not fix it. The demands have to come down. Named by Dora Raymaker.
- [Panic Hills of Low Object Permanence](https://monotropicmap.org/panic-hills-of-low-object-permanence): Out of sight, out of mind. Things, jobs and people you cannot see can drop away. Then you remember, and it is a shock. Named by Wenn Lawson.
- [Forest of Joy, Awe & Wonder](https://monotropicmap.org/forest-of-joy-awe-and-wonder): Happiness so big that your body has to move. Flapping, bouncing, dancing. This is one of the best parts of being Autistic. Named by Blackwater.
- [Lake of Limerence](https://monotropicmap.org/lake-of-limerence): You cannot stop thinking about one person. You do not know if they feel the same. The not knowing is what keeps it going. Named by Dorothy Tennov.
- [Tides of the Sensory Sea](https://monotropicmap.org/tides-of-the-sensory-sea): Sound, light, touch and smell come in strong. Some days much more than others. It is not a mood. It is your senses. Named by Janae Elisabeth.
- [Sudden Storms of Unexpected Events](https://monotropicmap.org/sudden-storms-of-unexpected-events): Something changes with no warning. You get pulled out of what you were doing. Your body reacts before you can think. Named by Kieran Rose.

## The nine zones of neuronormative domination
- [Mountains of Misinformation](https://monotropicmap.org/neuronormative-domination#mountains-of-misinformation): What a person has to climb before anybody will believe what they are telling them about their own mind. Decades of it, published, cited, and taught.
- [“Disorder” Framing Disaster Zone](https://monotropicmap.org/neuronormative-domination#disorder-framing-disaster-zone): Autism as a disorder: the framing built into the diagnostic manual, the funding, and the first sentence of most things ever written about us. It puts the fault inside the person before a conversation has started.
- [Harmful highway](https://monotropicmap.org/neuronormative-domination#harmful-highway): The one-way road running through the middle of the map, all of its arrows pointing the same way. Decades of research done from the outside, aimed at making Autistic people more normal rather than making the world more habitable.
- [Behaviourism Bay](https://monotropicmap.org/neuronormative-domination#behaviourism-bay): A theory of learning that reduces human beings to inputs and outputs, still running at scale in schools and clinics. Compliance is measured; the person is not asked.
- [Marsh of Masking](https://monotropicmap.org/neuronormative-domination#marsh-of-masking): It covers most of the landscape, and that is the point of putting it in the middle. Masking is a survival mechanism of suppressed needs that many Autistic people perform just to get through a day. It works, and it costs everything.
- [Sandstorm of Stigma](https://monotropicmap.org/neuronormative-domination#sandstorm-of-stigma): The weather that arrives with the label. It changes what a room assumes about a person before they have said anything, and it does not blow over.
- [Dunes of Deficit Metaphors](https://monotropicmap.org/neuronormative-domination#dunes-of-deficit-metaphors): The language itself. Deficit, impairment, symptom, severity, risk — vocabulary that turns a difference into a deficiency before the sentence has finished. The puzzle piece is here too.
- [Canyon of Cures & Eugenics](https://monotropicmap.org/neuronormative-domination#canyon-of-cures-and-eugenics): Where the money went. Vast sums invested in cures and in preventing Autistic people from existing at all, while the things Autistic people actually asked for went unfunded. This is the zone that is not a metaphor.
- [Destination Neurotypical Bay](https://monotropicmap.org/neuronormative-domination#destination-neurotypical-bay): Where the highway was always going. A person who has arrived is indistinguishable from their peers, and exhausted, and nobody is measuring the second part.
